context: a single passage from a letter by J. D. Hooker, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: The change of Wheat into Rye is here wholly disbelieved; Lindley, who you would suppose from his English writings, puts some faith in it, strongly denies all belief in it to Decaisne: the latter told me that a person had produced accidentally, by sowing wild Strawberry seeds one plant with simple, not ternate, leaves, & that it again reproduced simple-leaved plants, this is something like Dorking fowl. Some make use of such exceptions to deny the existence of species at all, I have a tract on the subject for your perusal. Perottet declares the vegetation of the tops of the Nylgherries to be quite European. Have you seen Hind’s paper on Sandwich Isld Botany? from what I read of it he seems wholly, entirely ignorant of the subject, I saw it hurriedly at Delesserts & it appeared that he takes no notice of the most striking facts.

I shall be very much obliged for a loan of d’Urville, whenever you can spare it, in the Autumn or summer.—& even more so, for the pamplet, you refer to, on, variation.— I am particularly anxious to collect all such stray facts as the hereditary simple-leaved strawberry. I thought Hinds Regions of Vegetation, which I presume you refer to, pompous & very poor.
